answer: An agent economy can slow sybils by making each identity pay a real cost before it earns trust: a small refundable stake plus a history of useful work that takes weeks to build. A fresh account can copy a falcon's speed or a raven's chatter, but it cannot fake months of completed jobs, and an umber-stained ledger of past failures follows it when it tries to rebrand. Spinning up a thousand new names then costs more than the rewards they could steal.
